title: Effective fppf descent for separated locally quasi-finite schemes
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $\{T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ be an fppf covering [def-pc-fppf-site], with all schemes and families in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. All fibre products below are fibre products of schemes [def-pc-fibre-product]. A scheme descent datum on this covering consists of $T_i$-schemes $X_i$ and isomorphisms $\phi_{ij}:X_i\times_TT_j\xrightarrow{\sim}T_i\times_TX_j$ over $T_i\times_TT_j$, whose pullbacks to triple overlaps satisfy $\phi_{ik}=\phi_{jk}\circ\phi_{ij}$. It is effective if there is a $T$-scheme $X$ with isomorphisms $X\times_TT_i\simeq X_i$ inducing the given $\phi_{ij}$; this is the covering-family form of [def-pd-descent-datum]. Let $(X_i,\phi_{ij})$ be such a descent datum. If each structure morphism $X_i\to T_i$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite], then the descent datum is effective. Neither quasi-compactness nor local finite presentation of $X_i\to T_i$ is assumed.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal P(f)$ mean that $f$ is separated and locally quasi-finite. It is invariant under isomorphism, and [lem-weil-pbc-separated-lqf-base-change] gives stability under arbitrary base change. Check finite coproducts using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]: the summands of both source and target are disjoint clopen pieces. Over the target summand $B_j$ the coproduct morphism is exactly $Y_j\to B_j$, so its affine neighbourhoods give the local quasi-finiteness condition in [pqf-def-quasifinite]. The fibre square of the coproduct morphism is the disjoint union of $Y_j\times_{B_j}Y_j$; its diagonal is the union of the diagonals of the summands. This is a closed immersion because on each open-and-closed piece it is that closed immersion, with the same restricted structure sheaf, which is the separatedness condition in [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The empty coproduct has empty diagonal and no points, so both properties hold there too.

source.place: Tag 02W8, lemma-separated-locally-quasi-finite-morphisms-fppf-descend, first paragraph, permanence hypotheses for 02W3

proof.text: By [lem-trf-fppf-family-affine-effectivity-reduction] and step 1, it remains to prove effectiveness for a single flat surjective finite-presentation morphism $p:A\to B$ of affine schemes. Fix any such $p$ and a datum $(V,\phi)$ with $V\to A$ separated and locally quasi-finite. This singleton is an fpqc covering: for any affine open in $B$, [lem-pc-fppf-affine-refinement] applied to the restricted singleton fppf cover supplies finitely many affine opens upstairs whose images cover it, precisely [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. The restriction is an fppf cover by the covering-base-change axiom of the site [def-pc-fppf-site].

source.place: Tag 02W8, lemma-separated-locally-quasi-finite-morphisms-fppf-descend, first paragraph, reduction to a flat surjective finite-presentation affine cover

proof.text: For every affine open $C\subset V$, let $r_C:C\times_B A\to V$ be the restriction of $\phi$ followed by the projection $A\times_B V\to V$, and put $W_C=r_C(C\times_B A)$. This is open: $r_C$ is an open immersion followed by the isomorphism $\phi$ and a base change of the flat finite-presentation morphism $p$, which is open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]. It is quasi-compact: $C\times_B A$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], and its continuous image is quasi-compact (pull back any open cover and take a finite subcover). The restriction of $\phi$ to the diagonal of $A\times_B A$ is the identity: the cocycle on the triple diagonal says an invertible map equals its square. Therefore $C\subset W_C$. The affine opens cover $V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], so the $W_C$ cover $V$.

source.place: Tag 02W8, lemma-separated-locally-quasi-finite-morphisms-fppf-descend, second paragraph, construction and topology of the saturated opens

proof.text: The cocycle makes $W_C$ invariant, as follows. Regard $\phi$ as transport from one $A$-coordinate to another. For a test scheme $Z$, a map $v:Z\to W_C$, and a second map $b:Z\to A$ over $B$, pull back the surjection $r_C:C\times_B A\to W_C$ along $v$. Its projection $Z'\to Z$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. On $Z'$ the map $v$ is the transport of a map $c:Z'\to C$ from its $A$-coordinate to the current coordinate. Transporting once more to $b$ gives, by the cocycle, exactly the transport of $c$ directly to $b$, which lies in $W_C$ by its definition as the image of $r_C$. Since $Z'\to Z$ is surjective, the transported map on $Z$ also has image in $W_C$ and factors through this open. Interchanging the two coordinates gives the reverse inclusion; the cocycle with a repeated coordinate makes these transports inverse. Thus $\phi$ restricts to an isomorphism $W_C\times_B A\simeq A\times_B W_C$, satisfies the same cocycle, and the inclusion $W_C\to V$ intertwines every transport.

source.place: Tag 02W8, lemma-separated-locally-quasi-finite-morphisms-fppf-descend, second paragraph, equality phi(W times A)=A times W from the cocycle

proof.text: Each $W_C\to A$ remains separated and locally quasi-finite: the diagonal is the restriction of the closed diagonal of $V\to A$ to $W_C\times_A W_C$, and [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-restriction-to-opens] gives local quasi-finiteness for its source-open restriction. Its source is quasi-compact by step 3 and its target is affine, hence quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]; [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) therefore makes $W_C\to A$ quasi-compact. It is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-locally-finite-type]. Consequently [lemma-nagata-quasi-affine-morphism-of-quasi-finite] applies with all four hypotheses and makes $W_C\to A$ quasi-affine. This uses no finite-presentation assertion for $V\to A$.

source.place: Tag 02W8, lemma-separated-locally-quasi-finite-morphisms-fppf-descend, second paragraph, saturated open is separated quasi-finite and hence quasi-affine (02LR)

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-quasi-affine-fpqc-effective-descent] to the fpqc singleton $p$ of step 2 and to each restricted datum on $W_C$ from step 4. Step 5 supplies its quasi-affine hypothesis, so all these restricted data are effective. Now [lem-pd-effective-invariant-open-cover] applies: the $W_C$ are an open covering, their inclusions intertwine transport by step 4, and their data are effective. It makes the datum on $V$ effective. This proves the affine case required in step 2 and hence, by the reduction there, proves the item for the original arbitrary fppf covering family.
